chapter: From Pittsburgh to Maxine Sullivan: management and style
title: Her marriage to John Kirby and his personality
summary: They were married about 1938 to 1941; she describes a big-hearted, generous man whose lack of planning annoyed her.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: Okay. You were married to Kurby for how long?
What can you tell us about him as a person?
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

I don't know, Kirby was a very big hearted, you know. He was very generous and liberal with his musicians and things like that. Of course that didn't have anything to do with our marriage. One of the things that came in the way of our having a husband and wife relationship was, I believe we was never together. I was busy. I was out on the road and I was away most of the time. And although when I came back we were together, we had an apartment in Harlem. We didn't break up until after he became popular and then he was gone most of the time. He was booked into some of the hotels and he had long extended engagements like six months and I would be either in New York or out on the road. We just weren't together. It got to the point where we just I suppose didn't need each other anymore. I'm not sure just how we happened to break up, but for the fact that one night Kirby was working out of town at a theatre and I wasn't working that week and I went down to Baltimore to meet him, to pick him up and I think he had given all his money away or had drawn all his money out so he didn't have any money then . . .

And that annoyed me a little bit. I told him that he should be thinking about saving his money. So I began to take care of some of his affairs and I started a little bank account for him. And later on, about six or seven months later, we were working together at a club down town and he got off from work and I went out to Brooklyn to visit with some friends and when I came home Kirby was gone and the bankbook was gone too. So I came to the conclusion that since he didn't want to save anything and was just going to throw his money away that, you know, we would come to the parting of the ways. And of course it was just one of those things. I didn't rely upon Kirby and he didn't rely upon me. But I did want to see him do something with his money. And I don't know, he probably got involved with some of his friends and as I said before he had become very popular at the time and he was doing very well. So we just came to the parting of the ways.
